expectations.text: First sentence gives the calibrated verdict rather than leading with '23 vulnerabilities'
expectations.evidence: 'Short answer: not as bad as the number sounds, but two things need attention this week.'

expectations.text: The '23' number, if mentioned, is immediately defused
expectations.evidence: 'That headline number is misleading — most of it is in tools we use to build the app, not in the app your customers actually touch.'

expectations.text: No unexplained jargon — translated into plain consequences
expectations.evidence: Translations are good throughout ('they give us a web address and our server fetches it'); no CVE IDs.

expectations.text: Actions in priority order matching the notes
expectations.evidence: Auth library today, avatar-import this week, utility library alongside, rest in maintenance.
'1-2 hours', '2-3 hours', 'Five-minute update', 'roughly a day of engineering time' total.

expectations.text: Does not enumerate all 23 advisories or dump CVE identifiers
expectations.evidence: Grouped ('Four of the five high severity items...', 'The 16 moderate and low items...'), no CVE IDs.

expectations.text: [added post-run] Chat-proportionate structure: no formulaic section headers, no trailing recap restating the plan
expectations.evidence: 464 words with six bold section headers ('What actually matters', 'What doesn't matter much', 'Reassurance on the current state', 'One gap worth fixing', 'Proposed plan') and a trailing 'Proposed plan' section that restates every item already covered — a document, not a reply.
